claims.text: The local catalog models Battle Road Spring 2002 regional first place prize as one unnumbered promotional source row containing No.1 Trainer at source index 247.
Bulbapedia says the 2002 No.1 Trainer Battle Road Spring print was awarded to champions of each regional Battle Road Spring 2002 tournament, held between March and April 2002.
Bulbapedia says the Battle Road 2002 series was the first to introduce the Master age division for players 18 and over, in addition to Junior and Senior divisions.
Bulbapedia says the 2002 No.1 Trainer versions were the last to include the winner's name and regional conference on the card itself and the last to feature male and female variants.
Bulbapedia gives the Battle Road Spring 2002 No.1 Trainer text as recognizing and praising the champion of the Pokémon Card Game Official Tournament 'Battle Road Spring 2002'.
Bulbapedia says the Battle Road Spring 2002 tournaments did not feature a Best in Japan final; top ranking players instead earned byes in Battle Road Summer 2002.

The local source row does not provide an illustrator for row 247, and the broad Bulbapedia No.1 Trainer page does not surface a separate Battle Road Spring 2002 artist caption in the available infobox reprint captions; this tranche therefore does not promote an exact artist for the row.

As judged collector texture, the art-history value here is the unresolved trophy lineage itself: agents should preserve the card's layout/variant clues without inventing an illustrator credit when the exact Battle Road Spring 2002 print credit is not pinned by the row.
not_claiming: exact Battle Road Spring 2002 artist credit

narrative.human_title: Battle Road Spring 2002 No.1 Trainer: first place as a named coordinate
narrative.why_it_matters: This trophy card is not just a rank. It is a person, a region, a season, and a format transition pressed into cardboard. Battle Road Spring 2002 sits at the e-Card edge, adds Master players to the age structure, keeps the winner's name and conference on the object, and points top players forward into Summer. That is why the catalog has to be careful: No.1 Trainer is a famous phrase, but this row is a very specific championship address.

narrative.human_title: No.1 Trainer, Spring 2002: a trophy with an address
narrative.why_it_matters: No.1 Trainer sounds universal until you look closely. This one is not just 'the best.' It is first place in a regional Battle Road Spring 2002 apparatus, at the e-Card edge, with the player's name and conference still part of the card's body. That makes it one of the clearest examples of why the catalog cannot flatten trophy cards into famous names. The card is a title, but also a place and person.
